subject: Updated subprocessor roster: Silverline caching proxy — evidence & EU egress clarifications
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@silverline.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: dpo@silverline.com
Date: Fri, 22 Jun 2028 14:12:00 +0000
Subject: Silverline notice: adding EdgeCacheX (caching proxy) — subprocessor info requested

Hi Jonas / Marissa,

Quick heads-up from Silverline: we plan to add a third-party caching proxy (EdgeCacheX Ltd.) to accelerate static content and thin telemetry for our Silverline CDN layer. Because this could interact with request metadata and short-lived KV entries, our privacy/security team asked for the following by EOD Tuesday:

- Your current subprocessor manifest that lists processors involved in handling Silverline traffic
- A short dataflow diagram showing routing for EU-origin traffic and whether any logs or telemetry are routed outside the EU
- Any evidence we can point to (SOC 2 type II report, encryption attestations) for EdgeCacheX or equivalent controls

We attach a Silverline intake form for your convenience. If EdgeCacheX performs only transient caching without storing PII, please state that explicitly — and confirm if you have an onshore fallback in EU regions.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Rossi
Privacy Program Manager
Silverline Tech

Attachment: silverline_vendor_intake.pdf (stub)

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@silverline.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 22 Jun 2028 15:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Silverline notice: adding EdgeCacheX (caching proxy) — subprocessor info requested

Elena —

Thanks for the flag and the intake form. Looping in Lauren (legal) to handle DPA/addendum language and Marissa for engineering specifics. Quick answers up-front:

- I attached our latest subprocessor manifest (subprocessor_manifest_v2.xlsx) and a simplified EU dataflow (dataflow-eu-diagram.png).
- EdgeCacheX is being proposed as an ephemeral caching tier; by default it does not persist PII. We will confirm precise logging retention windows.
- We can produce SOC 2 summary evidence for the caching vendor if required; please confirm the minimal scope you need (SOC 2, attestations for encryption in transit & at rest).

Action items: Lauren — can you review the draft addendum I’m attaching and advise on any EU egress clauses we should offer?

Elena — what timeline is Silverline working to? We can prioritize a tighter response if you need an exec-level attestation.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Head of Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: subprocessor_manifest_v2.xlsx; dataflow-eu-diagram.png

From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@silverline.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, dpo@silverline.com
Date: Fri, 22 Jun 2028 16:10:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Silverline notice: adding EdgeCacheX (caching proxy) — subprocessor info requested

Thanks Jonas — received both attachments and the quick note. Our timeline: we kick off a pilot next week (30 June) and need to complete legal & privacy checks before traffic is routed.

A couple of clarifying Qs from our DPO:
- You mention "no PII persistence" — can you confirm whether request headers or hashed identifiers are logged by EdgeCacheX and whether those logs may be replicated to US-based analytics?
- If logs do leave the EU, is there an automatic onshore fallback option to route EU-origin requests to an onshore caching node (or disable the partner caching for EU customers)?

If you can answer those two points and provide any SOC 2/security summary for EdgeCacheX, we should be able to sign a limited addendum.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

— Elena
Elena Rossi
Privacy Program Manager, Silverline Tech

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@silverline.com>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 23 Jun 2028 08:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Silverline notice: adding EdgeCacheX (caching proxy) — subprocessor info requested

Hi Elena —

Thanks for the callout and the follow-up questions. I reviewed the manifest Jonas attached and drafted a short addendum that addresses transient cache behavior, logging controls, and EU egress commitments. Summary of our position (high level):

- Classification: EdgeCacheX will be a transient caching subprocessor (no retention of customer PII beyond short TTLs).
- Logging: EdgeCacheX may create short-lived request logs for debugging/operational purposes; by default we will not replicate raw request logs outside EU for Silverline-origin traffic. Aggregated telemetry for capacity/latency may be exported (no PII).
- Onshore fallback: We will provide a configuration toggle to disable EdgeCacheX for EU routing or route EU-origin traffic to an onshore fallback pool managed by Redwood (and covered by our EU data residency controls).
- Evidence: we can provide a vendor security summary and redacted SOC 2 summary; full SOC 2 reports will be shared under NDA/secure link.

I attached a short DPA addendum draft (dpa_addendum_draft.docx) with the clauses we propose (egress clause, fallback SLA, logging limits, and audit rights). Please let us know if Silverline needs specific language for data export carve-outs or notification timelines (we proposed 30 days notice for subprocessor changes).

Next steps we propose:
1) Elena — confirm if Silverline requires the onshore fallback as mandatory or optional for the pilot.
2) If mandatory, we will enable the fallback and provide a secure link for SOC 2 evidence (we'll need a short NDA if you want the unredacted report).
3) If Silverline is OK with optional fallback, we'll include an explicit configuration and logging limits in the addendum and share the DocuSign link.

Happy to hop on a 30-minute call Monday to finalize language.

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Legal Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: dpa_addendum_draft.docx

From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@silverline.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, dpo@silverline.com
Date: Sat, 23 Jun 2028 09:20:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Silverline notice: adding EdgeCacheX (caching proxy) — subprocessor info requested

Lauren / Jonas —

Appreciate the clear summary and the draft addendum. For the pilot Silverline requires the onshore fallback to be enabled for EU-origin traffic and we will accept a redacted SOC 2 summary via secure link (NDA OK).

Please send the DocuSign link for the addendum and the secure SOC 2 access instructions. I’ll loop in procurement for the paperwork. If you can enable the fallback today for a no-risk test, that would help accelerate our pilot.

Thanks — Elena

--
Elena Rossi
Privacy Program Manager
Silverline Tech
